chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Ibn Muskān from al-Ḥalabī said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Any food that you have specified with a measure (kayl), it is not suitable for gharar (uncertainty/speculation).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling food with a specified measure to avoid uncertainty (gharar)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that designating a specific measure (kayl) for food items validates the transaction against gharar, ensuring the commodity is clearly defined. This ruling, found in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on precision in commercial contracts to prevent dispute and uncertainty. It reflects the broader principle that explicit quantification removes the element of speculation inherent in sales of bulk goods.
